alert.title: cart p99 latency 3.4s — cart-db connection saturation suspected

tool_calls.result_summary: no deploys in last 24h to cart or cart-db
pool utilization climbed from 62% to 100% over 30 min, plateaued
14 FATAL lines: 'too many connections' on cart-db replica 2
runbook documents pool resize + restart of largest cart pod

hypotheses.reasoning: cart-db connection pool saturated at 100% with 14 FATAL 'too many connections' log lines. cart latency tracks the saturation curve. No recent deploys to cart or cart-db, so this is capacity-driven rather than a regression. Most likely a long-running query or leaked connection on a cart-db client.

evidence.claim: cart-db pool utilization plateaued at 100% from 13:32 onwards
14 FATAL 'too many connections' lines on cart-db replica 2
No deploys to cart or cart-db in the last 24h

hypotheses.recommended_action: Bump cart-db pool size and restart the largest cart pod to free connections; see runbooks/cart.md

hypotheses.reasoning: cart itself is the alerting service, but its code is unchanged and its CPU/memory are at baseline. Latency is a downstream symptom.

evidence.claim: cart CPU and memory at baseline; only latency spiked

hypotheses.recommended_action: Do not roll back cart — fix the cart-db pool first.

hypotheses.reasoning: An unrelated workload could be hammering cart-db, but no evidence of cross-service writes appears in the logs.

evidence.claim: logs show only cart-originating queries on cart-db replica 2

hypotheses.recommended_action: Check cart-db query top-N if pool fix does not resolve.

escalation.reason: Documented runbook applies; capacity action is reversible.
